turns.t: Oh, I'm so sorry I'm late, doctor, the bus broke down by the chemist and then the driver let us all off, and I had to walk past my sister's house, she's just had a new kitchen, you should see it. ~
Not to worry. Come and sit down. What's brought you in today? ~
My heart. It races. Palpitations, the pharmacist called it. It happens after I've had too much coffee.
Tell me about it. What does it feel like?
Like a little bird in my chest, thumping and fluttering. It goes on for a few minutes, then it settles.
How much coffee are we talking about? ~
Five or six cups, on busy days. I'm a big believer in a good flat white. And an energy drink in the afternoon, if I'm honest. ~
That's a lot of caffeine. Do you feel anything else when it happens?
My hands go jittery. I can't hold a pen.
Have you had any chest pain?
No chest pain. Never.
When did you last have an episode? ~
Tuesday, at work. I'd had four coffees before ten. My colleague said I'd gone pale. ~
And what do you do when it happens? ~
I sit down and drink water. And then I wonder if I'm dying. My mum gets the same, you know, she's a worrier. ~
I understand. Let me explain what I think is happening. Caffeine is a stimulant, it makes the heart beat faster and more forcefully. ~
So it's the coffee? ~
Most likely, yes. The pattern fits, it comes after the coffee, settles in minutes, and you feel shaky as well. I think caffeine is the most likely trigger.
Do I have to give it up completely? ~
Not completely. Cut it to two cups a day, and drop the energy drinks. Do it gradually over a week, so you don't get a headache.
That's going to be a tough week. ~
I'd also like to give you propranolol, 10 mg, to take when it happens, up to twice a day.
Is it addictive? ~
No, not at all. It calms the heart down. Don't take it if you're wheezy or have asthma. ~
No asthma here. ~
Good. Keep a note of when the episodes happen and what you've had.
I'll do a diary. I love a diary. ~
If they carry on after two weeks of cutting down the coffee, come back and see me.
I will. Thank you so much, doctor, you've been so kind. And do try the new kitchen place, my sister's... ~
Take care. ~
Cheerio. ~
